A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, model, and original experiments. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on a parametric simulation, noisy Swiss roll, colored MNIST, CelebA-Glasses, and single-cell RNA-sequencing data, including quantitative results and visual analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds disentanglement analyses, component ablations, CelebA-Hats results, and computational resource measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed dual-latent architecture, two reconstructions, max–min objective, learned conditional prior, and Algorithm 1 are retained. DISCoVeR becomes DisCoVR. MLP classifiers mentioned in v2's main text were already documented in v1's appendix; the added classifier and prior variants serve as controlled ablations.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds disentanglement using CelebA's Wearing hat attribute, extending the retained eyeglasses task to another attribute. All original datasets and noise scenarios remain; this is a limited task extension within an existing image domain.

E2.justification: Existing baseline membership is preserved in corresponding comparisons, and CelebA-Hats reuses existing baselines. The supplementary parametric comparison adds DisCoVR with a CSVAE-style prior and an untruncated-posterior reference, locally expanding the comparison set in Supplementary Tables 4–7.

E3.justification: Appendix E substantially expands evaluation with kNN estimation at k=20, additional label/latent and conditional mutual-information metrics, MIG, MIC, and rankings by proximity to ground truth. Reported parametric-model reconstruction, KL(z), and z-only reconstruction weights also change from 0.7/0.7/0.3 to 0.75/0.9/0.25, although Table 1's numbers remain unchanged; rerunning is not established.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's noise sweeps and posterior visualizations, Appendix F directly tests classifier placement and replacement of the learned conditional prior with a standard Gaussian on Swiss roll and colored MNIST. Appendix E adds a separable-prior variant and comparisons across information estimators and ground-truth targets. These substantially expand scrutiny of the model's components and evaluation sensitivity.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations over ten experiments with different seeds, so no increase in repetitions is established. v2 newly reports standard deviations for Swiss-roll mutual information in Table 2 and explicitly identifies CelebA-Hats as a single experiment without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Most original benchmark numbers remain unchanged. Swiss-roll Table 2 revises mutual information, including DIVA from 0.423 to 0.336 and CCVAE from 0.254 to 0.502, reversing their ordering. Supplementary Tables 4–15 and Figures 7–8 add extensive metric, ablation, resource, and hat-attribute results. These are added or revised reports, rather than demonstrated improvements of the method between versions.

T1.justification: Proposition 2.1 and Appendix B.1 restore the missing expectation over q(w|x,y) around the KL gap. Appendix E introduces MIG and MIC definitions, while Section 3 adds an optimization implication concerning a mutual-information lower bound. The original model assumptions and Proposition 2.2 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: dual representations and reconstructions, a max–min formulation with a unique equilibrium, and improved disentanglement across synthetic, image, and biological data. Rewording and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 expands explanations of information allocation under joint reconstruction, separable versus flexible priors, and agreement between information estimators. Appendix F adds interpretations concerning classifier tuning and collapse under an unconditional prior. The conclusion removes v1's explicit limitation to fully observed, discrete condition labels, without establishing broader applicability.

D1.justification: Supplementary Tables 13–15 add training time, inference time, and memory measurements, and the parametric loss-weight documentation changes. v1's public GitHub pointer is replaced by a statement that code accompanies the submission and will become public upon acceptance. Most architecture, optimizer, hardware, and other implementation specifications are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes the empirical-Bayes/f-modeling positioning and references to Robbins and Efron, and adds Kraskov et al. for kNN information estimation. Section 4 expands the positioning around separate reconstruction, the conditional prior, and conditional-independence requirements. The principal competing approaches and broader related-work coverage remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively condensed and rewritten, method and comparison explanations are revised, and the acronym changes throughout the prose. Dedicated appendices for additional metrics, ablations, and CelebA-Hats precede implementation details, which move from Appendix E to H. The narrative revisions extend well beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: v2 adds Supplementary Tables 4–15, including grouped metric tables and colored ranking displays, plus ablation Figures 7–8. Existing displays are retained with resizing, relocation, and expanded captions, particularly Figures 3–5. The title, headings, headers, and overall document formatting also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The corrected Proposition 2.1, component ablations, and computational measurements improve correctness and scrutiny. However, Section 3 newly claims that maximizing a mutual-information lower bound maximizes the information itself, which does not follow from the stated bound; Appendix E's ranking-consistency claim is also contradicted by differences between Supplementary Tables 10–11. Alongside removal of the public code pointer and explicit label-scope limitation, these gains and harms leave the net quality direction uncertain.
